source.title: Advancing underwater acoustic target recognition via adaptive data pruning and smoothness-inducing regularization
source.authors: Yuan Xie; Tian-Yu Chen; Ji Xu

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a test-loss curve over training for an underwater acoustic recognition model, a different setting from the original studies. It does not sweep model size or sample count.
record.gate_note: Figure 1(b) and its accompanying text report double descent in the baseline model's test loss during training. The data-pruning accuracy comparisons are retained as a related finding under fits_no_version: they report classification accuracy, not the double-descent curve. Cited results from other work are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: Fig. 1(b) reports a test-loss curve over training epochs for the baseline ResNet+attention on ship-radiated noise, which the authors say shows clear double descent. That is a result on V2 in a new setting (underwater acoustic recognition). It is figure-only. The rest of the paper reports accuracy gains from pruning and regularization, not double-descent curves. No model-size or sample-size sweep is done.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that periodic repetition in ship-radiated signals causes double descent and performance degradation, and that adaptive data pruning addresses this effectively and efficiently. They add that smoothness-inducing regularization beats data augmentation and GANs, and that the combined pipeline exceeds SOTA on Shipsear (88.79% vs 85.48%).
record.recipe_differences: The study examines test loss over training in underwater acoustic recognition and uses adaptive pruning of similar segments; it does not reproduce the original model-size or sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported pruning-related accuracy varies across dataset, acoustic feature, and regularization method; the study does not report these as changes in the double-descent curve.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors attribute the epoch-wise double descent to highly similar or repeated training segments, and say pruning them eliminates it. Only an accuracy improvement is shown, with no curve values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated or near-duplicate training samples induce epoch-wise double descent, and pruning them removes it.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning similar segments raised accuracy in every dataset × feature × regularization setting in Table 1. It also cut training time by 11–65% (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive pruning of similar acoustic segments improves recognition accuracy and efficiency.

record.problems: The epoch-wise curve is reported without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The study does not provide a model-size or sample-size sweep.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also lists benchmark/SOTA results not representing pruning comparisons; these are not results on the tested double-descent curve. Cited findings from other work are excluded.

untested.parts: No numeric curve, peak location, or link of the peak to the interpolation threshold.
No label-noise or tuned-regularization analysis of the peak. No post-pruning or post-regularization curve is reported numerically.

missing.what: Whether Fig. 1(b) also shows a post-pruning or post-regularization test-loss curve. The caption mentions optimization brought by the methods, which bears on removing the double-descent peak.
Table 1 Mel smooth-reg rows (Shipsear 82.76→88.79; DeepShip 77.05→78.77) and the other DeepShip Mel rows are not recorded. These are accuracy only, not version-bearing.

record.verdict_notes: The epoch-wise double-descent evidence is a single figure described in words; it is weak support. Table 1 text is garbled. Table 2 shows Mel rows of 77.14, 77.68, 77.72 and 82.76, which implies four method rows per feature. The reader's condition labels for r2–r19 therefore appear shifted, but this does not affect any version verdict. Tranche changed from T2 to T3: the measure matches the original's test loss over epochs, and the novelty is the acoustic setting.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and peak near the size that just fits the training set.
The reported curve is for the baseline setting; the text does not provide a numeric curve or separately report a post-pruning epoch-wise curve.
No sweep that increases training sample count near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison of double descent across model classes.
No unified effective-complexity measure or prediction of peak locations.
No test of label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization eliminating the peak.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters.
